chunks: Al-Saffar, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far عليه السلام, that Ali عليه السلام used to say:
“There is no qisas in a bone.”
And Ja'far عليه السلام said: “A man killed a woman, so Ali عليه السلام did not establish qisas between them, and he obligated him to pay the diyah.”

key_terms.أَلْزَمَهُ: he obligated him; indicating legal imposition by judicial authority
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money; the prescribed financial compensation
key_terms.امْرَأَةً: a woman; the female victim in the reported legal case
key_terms.رَجُلًا: a man; the male party in the reported legal case
key_terms.عَظْمٍ: bone; the bodily injury mentioned here as not subject to qisas
key_terms.قِصَاصٌ: retaliatory legal retribution in injury or killing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on qisas for bone injury and when a man kills a woman according to Imam Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning qisas in cases involving bone injury and a case of a man killing a woman. It reports that Amir al-Mu'minin Ali عليه السلام did not apply qisas between them in that case and instead imposed the diyah, indicating a juridical distinction in such matters.
